zh-CN.Distinguish screw withdrawal from latera: Distinguish screw withdrawal from lateral resistance, derive an illustrative force couple, and design connection checks around the actual load path.
zh-CN.Ask What the Connection Must Transfer: Ask What the Connection Must Transfer
zh-CN.A screw may be pulled along its axis, lo: A screw may be pulled along its axis, loaded across its axis, or participate in an assembly that combines these actions. Rammer's Wood Handbook Chapter 8 [1] discusses withdrawal and lateral resistance separately and explains why wood properties and joint geometry matter. This article uses that distinction to build a simple load-path example. It does not provide design capacities or approve hardware. Its research question is narrower: what information disappears when a maker replaces a connection drawing with a statement such as four screws should be enough? The answer begins with force direction and the location of the applied load.
zh-CN.The handbook's Wood Screws section ties: The handbook's Wood Screws section ties its equations to particular fastener dimensions, penetration, wood properties, and lead-hole conditions. It also distinguishes research results from design values modified for service and safety. Therefore a quoted experimental maximum should retain its conditions and should not become an allowable load for a different screw or substrate. An edge connection in particleboard is a different case from a side-grain connection in solid wood. The defensible starting point is the specific fastener system's documentation, together with the actual material and installation geometry.
zh-CN.Suppose an idealized bracket carries a d: Suppose an idealized bracket carries a downward force F = 200 N whose line of action lies e = 150 mm in front of a wall. The applied moment is M = Fe = 30,000 N·mm, or 30 N·m. Imagine that an upper tensile reaction and a lower compressive bearing reaction form a couple separated vertically by h = 100 mm. In this simplified equilibrium model, the tensile reaction is T = M/h = 300 N. The vertical reaction must still transfer 200 N. These numbers describe assumed external equilibrium; they are not measured screw actions or allowable connection loads.
zh-CN.A Spacing Change Reveals the Missing Var: A Spacing Change Reveals the Missing Variable
zh-CN.If the idealized reaction separation bec: If the idealized reaction separation becomes 200 mm while the same load and eccentricity remain, the couple requires 150 N rather than 300 N. This inverse relationship explains why two connection drawings with the same screw count can ask different things of their fasteners. It does not imply that doubling screw spacing doubles the capacity of a real bracket. Flexibility, prying, fastener position, bearing contact, edge distances, and substrate behavior can alter the distribution. A real connection also needs the correct treatment of combined actions. Preserve the simple model as a screening sketch, then resolve the actual system.
zh-CN.Why Equal Sharing Is an Assumption: Why Equal Sharing Is an Assumption
zh-CN.Even when two upper screws appear symmet: Even when two upper screws appear symmetric, dividing the tensile reaction equally requires a load-sharing model. Clearance in one hole, imperfect contact, a flexible plate, or installation damage may concentrate action before the other screw engages. For that reason, keep the total reaction visible in the notes before any allocation to individual screws. List the evidence supporting the allocation and any uncertainty. The same reasoning applies to vertical shear: a shelf resting on a support may transfer some force through bearing, whereas a hanging component may ask its screws to transfer it directly.
zh-CN.Record Installation as Part of the Speci: Record Installation as Part of the Specimen
zh-CN.For a proposed controlled connection stu: For a proposed controlled connection study, record screw model, threaded penetration, hole preparation, substrate identity, thickness, grain or panel direction, edge distance, and installation procedure. Distinguish tightening control from ultimate strength: installation torque is not a direct measurement of withdrawal resistance. Use separate specimens for destructive tests and document the loading fixture, rate, and observed failure mode. Reusing a hole changes the specimen. Count independent connections rather than treating repeated loading of the same damaged joint as independent trials. Any service recommendation requires the applicable product and design basis beyond this proposed study.
zh-CN.Put the Load Path Beside the Part List: Put the Load Path Beside the Part List
zh-CN.A useful cabinet release sheet identifie: A useful cabinet release sheet identifies the supported component, the load location, the bracket or joint, the substrate, and where reactions enter the surrounding structure. Link the current hardware instructions and record the document revision. Keep a fastener schedule with the assembly rather than burying it in a generic shopping note. If a dimensional revision reduces usable penetration or moves a hole toward an edge, reopen the connection review. The optimization software can place a panel on a sheet, but that success supplies no evidence about the hardware holding the installed component.
zh-CN.The arithmetic establishes that an offse: The arithmetic establishes that an offset load creates a moment and that an ideal force couple depends on its separation. It does not determine actual fastener sharing, pull-through resistance, wall anchorage, splitting, or capacity under sustained loading. A complete review follows the load through every interface rather than stopping at the screw head. Where product data or substrate identification is missing, the next useful action is to obtain that evidence. Replacing missing evidence with the highest published laboratory number would answer a different question from the one the installed connection presents.
Draw the applied force and its offset.

zh-CN.Applied moments, bearing, geometry, and: Applied moments, bearing, geometry, and installation determine the actions at the connection. A screw count does not describe that load path.
